description: Critical care news shown on /news, newest first. Add items only after Kenil approves them in chat. Fields: id, date (YYYY-MM-DD), tag (Guideline | Trial | India | Drug safety | Review), source, title, summary, url, moduleId (optional, links the item to a module), catchUp (optional, true for older items published as catch-up).

items.title: A simple bedside index may flag patients who won't respond to more noradrenaline
items.summary: VNERi = diastolic BP ÷ (noradrenaline dose × heart rate). In a secondary analysis of 391 patients in ANDROMEDA-SHOCK, a baseline VNERi below 2.6 went with 28-day mortality of 50% vs 28.8%. In that group, raising the noradrenaline dose barely moved the MAP (−0.17 vs +4.43 mmHg per 0.1 µg/kg/min). It's a prompt to think early about adding a second agent, but it still needs prospective testing.

items.title: Pre-existing clonal haematopoiesis (CHIP) was linked to worse sepsis outcomes
items.summary: In a retrospective biobank study of 3,230 ICU sepsis patients, CHIP found on DNA taken before the illness went with higher ICU mortality (OR 1.54), fewer days free of vasopressors, ventilation and dialysis, and higher long-term mortality among survivors (HR 1.40). It's background reading for now, not a bedside change.

items.title: Scrub typhus is still active in November, in Uttar Pradesh and Assam
items.summary: Sonbhadra (UP) has had 14 cases this year and has put PHCs and CHCs on alert. A 68-year-old man in Bongaigaon, Assam, has also died after being referred to a private hospital. Keep scrub typhus on the list for undifferentiated fever with organ dysfunction, look for an eschar, and start doxycycline early.

items.title: Puducherry: two recent dengue deaths and a rise in cases this year
items.summary: A 19-year-old and a 23-year-old have died of dengue in Puducherry in the last few days. The UT has had 1,362 cases this year (1,232 in the Puducherry region), including 46 in the first 19 days of November, with October and November accounting for 721 cases. Watch for warning signs and resuscitate dengue shock with cautious fluids.

items.title: ECPR anticoagulation varies widely between centres
items.summary: A EuroELSO/ESICM survey (186 responses, 41 countries) found 62% routinely give a ~5,000 IU UFH bolus at cannulation, and 17% omit it. UFH is used after cannulation in 89%. aPTT and anti-Xa targets vary widely, and many centres use lower targets in the first 24 h than general ECMO guidance. There's no standard yet, so follow your unit protocol.

items.title: Manipur: suspected toxic liquor deaths, with many patients in ICU and on dialysis
items.summary: The death toll in Manipur's suspected spurious liquor tragedy reached 17 (16 from Chandel, 1 from Kakching), with 228 of about 1,130 people screened still in hospital and 38 on dialysis. Samples have gone to labs in Imphal and Kolkata, so the cause is not yet confirmed, but think methanol if there is visual change, a high anion-gap acidosis or coma. Fomepizole (or ethanol) and early dialysis can be lifesaving.

items.title: Writing a review date on an ICU antibiotic prescription made a timely review much more likely
items.summary: A UK and Isle of Man audit of 2,626 patients in 154 ICUs found 60.6% were on antimicrobials. 92.7% of eligible orders were reviewed within 72 h, and a pre-specified stop or review date was strongly associated with that review (adjusted OR 9.3). A review date was written on only 66% of orders. The authors recommend putting a review date on every prescription.

items.title: Kerala: leptospirosis deaths and dengue are rising as flu eases
items.summary: Ernakulam has had 3 leptospirosis deaths and 21 confirmed cases in November so far, plus 481 dengue cases (114 confirmed). For fever with jaundice, AKI or lung haemorrhage, think lepto and start antibiotics early.

items.title: FDA early alert: some vascular guidewires pulled because the coating can flake
items.summary: Heraeus Medevio is recalling certain lots of the Navilyst and Spectrum vascular guidewires (H965457461, H965457471) and the Arrow Marked Guidewire (PW-18080-HN, PW-16130-HN). The hydrophilic coating can clump and shed particles into the bloodstream, which could cause emboli. No injuries or deaths have been reported. If your central line or access kits use these, check the lot numbers and quarantine affected stock. It is not confirmed whether these lots reached India.

items.title: ICU noise peaks were linked to next-day delirium, but light wasn't
items.summary: In 300 patients, with sound recorded every 5 seconds, each extra dBA the day before raised the risk of next-day delirium (aHR 1.11), and so did each extra 10 min/day above 70 dBA (aHR 1.18). Light showed no link, and the primary analysis was neutral, so the result only generates hypotheses. Still, it supports cutting night-time alarms and noise.

items.title: ICP-guided care was linked to lower ICU mortality in severe TBI
items.summary: A CENTER-TBI target-trial analysis of 773 patients with GCS < 9 and a CT abnormality compared ICP-guided care with care guided by imaging and examination. Centres that used ICP monitoring more often had lower ICU mortality (OR 0.7), including in patients with one or two unreactive pupils (OR 0.6). This is observational, so it may reflect a more aggressive overall approach, but it argues against writing these patients off early.

items.title: Prehospital 1-hour septic shock bundle did not lower mortality
items.summary: In a French cluster-randomised trial (381 patients), ambulance ICU teams gave antibiotics, saline up to 35 mL/kg, norepinephrine and hydrocortisone if needed. 28-day mortality was 22% vs 27% (RR 0.81, p = 0.16), not significant. Start the bundle early, but don't expect the ambulance phase alone to save lives.

items.title: Sepsis steroid systematic reviews often disagree, because they pool different trials
items.summary: A meta-research study of 42 systematic reviews (121 RCTs) found that more than half of review pairs shared no RCTs. Of 38 reviews that meta-analysed short-term mortality, 15 (39%) reported benefit and 23 (61%) found no effect. Discordance was limited to broad, non-specific steroid strategies; reviews of hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone consistently found benefit, and reviews of HAT (hydrocortisone, ascorbic acid and thiamine) consistently found none. When you read a review, check which trials it included.

items.title: Thrombectomy reaches 24-72 h strokes and mild strokes with a large-vessel occlusion
items.summary: LATE-MT (336 patients with salvageable tissue on imaging) found better 90-day function with thrombectomy (common OR 1.74), though symptomatic bleeds (4.8% vs 0%) and deaths (6.0% vs 1.8%) were higher. A second NEJM trial in mild strokes with a large-vessel occlusion found good outcomes in 69.4% vs 50.0% (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42929671/). Late presenters with an occlusion still deserve an urgent stroke-team call.

items.title: NEJM's new ARDS review (Calfee and McAuley)
items.summary: Sets both current ARDS definitions side by side. Core care is unchanged: treat the cause, ventilate lung-protectively, avoid fluid overload, and use prone positioning or ECMO in selected patients. A good teaching reference for the ARDS module.

items.title: A normal creatinine at ICU discharge can hide kidneys that haven't recovered
items.summary: In 137 patients after KDIGO stage 2 or 3 AKI who left ICU with a "normal" creatinine, iohexol clearance was still below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² in 51%. CKD-EPI eGFR caught this in only 19% of those patients. The group with hidden low GFR had a lower eGFR at 6 months. Don't assume recovery from a normal discharge creatinine alone.

items.source: The Indian Express (ICMR AMRSN Annual Report 2025)
items.title: ICMR AMRSN 2025: resistance is now the norm in ICU gram-negatives
items.summary: The report reviewed 1,13,008 isolates from 30 tertiary hospitals, plus 20,529 from 34 secondary-care hospitals for the first time. Only 36.5–40.4% of Klebsiella pneumoniae were susceptible to carbapenems (lower still in ICU), and 91.1% of Acinetobacter baumannii were carbapenem-resistant. E. coli susceptibility was 18.4% to cefotaxime and 9% to ciprofloxacin. Culture first, and save last-line drugs. The primary ICMR report page was still unavailable after the 21–22 Nov site maintenance, so this links to the Indian Express coverage.

items.title: Sepsis immune score may predict who benefits from hydrocortisone
items.summary: The Innate Immunity Score (5 cohorts, 1,267 patients) tracked severity and mortality. Hydrocortisone looked harmful when the score was low (69% of patients) and helpful when it was high. Hypothesis-generating only; it doesn't change practice yet.

items.title: About 1 in 100 pregnant or postpartum women need ICU care
items.summary: A meta-analysis of 50 studies (20 countries, 49,299 ICU admissions) found 1.0% need ICU care: 4.1% in low-income vs 0.5% in high-income countries. 72% had direct obstetric causes, mainly hypertension (26.9%) and haemorrhage (23.3%); ICU mortality was 8.5%. For Indian ICUs: catch pre-eclampsia and PPH early. Highlighted by ICMR-NIRWoH.

items.title: PANTHER: precision-medicine ARDS trial begins
items.summary: A blood test sorts patients into hyper- or hypo-inflammatory ARDS, who then get usual care, or usual care plus simvastatin or baricitinib, in an adaptive platform trial. It is the first big test of treating ARDS by biological subtype.

items.title: Cefazolin backed over cloxacillin for MSSA bacteraemia
items.summary: A Bayesian meta-analysis of the SNAP and CloCeBa trials (1,579 patients) gave a 95.5% probability that cefazolin is non-inferior for 90-day mortality (OR 0.84), with fewer treatment stops for adverse events (OR 0.25) and less AKI (OR 0.54). The authors conclude cefazolin should be preferred for adults with MSSA bacteraemia.

items.title: Oliceridine matched remifentanil for analgesia in ventilated patients, with less respiratory depression
items.summary: In CO-ROAM (304 ventilated adults in 19 Chinese ICUs), time in the target analgesic range was 96.0% vs 92.3% (non-inferior). Respiratory depression was 0% vs 4.6% during the study and 0% vs 7.9% after extubation. Ventilator days, ICU stay and 28-day mortality were the same. A useful option where it is available; it does not change usual care where it is not.

items.title: Cefepime didn't cause more delirium or neurotoxicity than pip-taz or meropenem
items.summary: This emulated-trial analysis matched 4,447 pairs (cefepime vs piperacillin-tazobactam) and 1,262 pairs (cefepime vs meropenem). Delirium or neurotoxicity rates were the same (RR 0.99 and 1.09), and so were 30-day mortality and length of stay. Neurotoxicity fear alone shouldn't drive the empirical choice, though dosing in renal failure still matters. The study is observational and from the US.

items.title: Community CPR and AED programme did not improve arrest survival
items.summary: In a cluster-randomised trial across North Carolina counties (22,459 patients), dispatcher training, community CPR training and wider AED use did not improve survival to discharge with good neurological outcome (9.0% vs 9.4%). Bystander CPR and early defibrillation remain standard; the lesson is that rolling these out widely needs better implementation strategies.

items.source: NEJM (OnScene, presented at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026)
items.title: ECPR started at the scene doubles survival in young adults with refractory arrest
items.summary: Dutch helicopter teams able to start VA-ECMO at the scene had 40% survival to discharge vs 20% with conventional care in adults aged 50 or under with refractory out-of-hospital arrest (good neurological outcome at 6 months: 36% vs 13%). The study was non-randomised and the patients were highly selected, so it supports fast ECPR referral pathways, not routine ECPR for every arrest.

items.title: Ulinastatin gave no survival benefit in sepsis (ADJUST)
items.summary: In the ADJUST RCT, 335 ICU adults with sepsis received IV ulinastatin 400,000 IU every 8 hours or placebo for up to 10 days. 28-day mortality was 23.6% vs 22.9% (HR 1.03). Secondary outcomes were the same, and adverse events were more common with ulinastatin (56.8% vs 42.7%). Routine ulinastatin for sepsis is not supported.

items.title: Centre proposes instant licence suspension for substandard drugs
items.summary: The Union health ministry has notified a proposal to immediately suspend a manufacturer's licence for a drug found 'not of standard quality' on assay, dissolution, impurities or sterility, removing the current show-cause delay. CDSCO's September 2026 alert listed 330 such samples, including a ciprofloxacin product that failed its assay test. This is still a proposal, so keep checking CDSCO's monthly alerts against your ICU pharmacy stock.

items.source: Intensive Care Medicine (highlighted by ESICM, 13 Nov)
items.title: Sodium bicarbonate: no clear survival benefit, but fewer patients need dialysis
items.summary: Pooling 4 RCTs (1,544 patients, including SODa-BIC and BICARICU-2), bicarbonate did not clearly reduce mortality (RR 0.94) but had a 97% probability of reducing RRT initiation (RR 0.74). This supports selective use in severe acidaemia with AKI, in line with SSC 2026, while watching for high sodium, low calcium and alkalosis.

items.title: Adding dobutamine during septic-shock source-control surgery cut AKI
items.summary: A multicentre RCT of 584 patients in 39 hospitals in China found intraoperative dobutamine plus norepinephrine lowered new or worsening AKI within 7 days from 34.7% to 22.8% (aRR 0.64), compared with norepinephrine alone. There was more tachycardia, but no rise in cardiac events, mortality or dialysis. The authors call it hypothesis-generating, so it isn't a practice change yet.

items.title: Starting vasopressin earlier did not reduce septic shock mortality
items.summary: Across 13 hospitals (3,959 patients), a strategy of starting vasopressin at noradrenaline-equivalent 0.1 µg/kg/min did not lower 28-day mortality compared with 0.4 µg/kg/min (31.8% vs 33.0%), and kidney replacement-free days were the same. This adds data to the vasopressin trigger dose that SSC 2026 leaves open.

items.title: Intermittent haemodialysis first linked to higher mortality than CRRT in ICU AKI
items.summary: In 535 critically ill patients with AKI needing RRT, starting with intermittent haemodialysis was not non-inferior to CRRT for major adverse kidney events. It was also associated with higher 90-day mortality (63.1% vs 53.5%; HR 1.30). The trial was stopped early, so treat the size of the effect with caution, but it supports CRRT as the first modality in unstable patients.

items.title: ICMR fungal registry: invasive fungal infection in Indian ICUs carries >50% mortality
items.summary: Among 178,417 admissions to 63 ICUs at eight ICMR Advanced Mycology centres (2023–25), 2,500 invasive fungal infections were found (14 per 1,000 admissions). All-cause mortality was 53.6%. Invasive candidiasis was most common (57.1%), then aspergillosis (37%) and mucormycosis (3.4%). The findings support rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship.
